text: In the book's treatment of the Kerr black hole, inside the ergosphere the time Killing vector ∂_t becomes spacelike. The physical consequence is that:
choices: an observer can still hover at rest relative to the distant stars
the observer has necessarily crossed the event horizon and can never escape
no observer can remain static; every observer must co-rotate with the hole
the Kretschmann curvature scalar necessarily diverges there
explanation: With g_tt > 0 inside the ergosphere, staying at fixed (r, θ, φ) is impossible, so frame dragging forces every observer to co-rotate with the black hole. Crucially the ergosphere lies OUTSIDE the outer event horizon r_+ (they touch only at the poles), so observers can still enter and leave it — that is what enables the Penrose process — and the curvature there remains finite.
